items.question_text: A block of mass 5 kg sits on a horizontal table. A pulley is fixed at each edge of the table, one on the left and one on the right. A string from the block goes left over the left pulley and down to a hanging block of mass 15 kg; call its tension T₂. Another string from the block goes right over the right pulley and down to a hanging block of mass 5 kg; call its tension T₁. The coefficient of friction between the table and the 5 kg block on it is 0.2. What is the ratio T₁ : T₂ (tension in the right string to tension in the left string)?
items.figure_description: A block of mass 5 kg rests on a horizontal table. A pulley sits fixed at the left edge of the table and another at the right edge. The string on the left, labeled T₂, runs from the block over the left pulley and down to a hanging 15 kg block. The string on the right, labeled T₁, runs from the block over the right pulley and down to a hanging 5 kg block.

items.question_text:
A block sits on a rough incline that rises at 30° to the horizontal. A string tied to the block is pulled at 30° above the incline surface. Draw a diagram showing every force acting on the block, and resolve each of these forces:
(a) Find the horizontal and vertical components of each force.
(b) Find the components of each force parallel and perpendicular to the incline surface.
items.figure_description: An incline rises to the right at 30° to the horizontal ground, with a block resting on its surface. Four forces act on the block: N, the normal reaction, perpendicular to the incline surface and pointing away from it; T, the tension in the string, pointing up the slope and away from the surface at 30° above the incline surface (so T makes 60° with N and 60° with the horizontal); w, the weight, acting straight down; and f, friction, acting down along the incline surface (toward the lower end of the slope).

items.question_text: A block of mass m lies at rest on a slope inclined at angle θ to the horizontal; the coefficient of friction between block and slope is μ. Find the magnitude of the resultant contact force (normal reaction and friction combined) that the slope applies to the block.

Assertion: For a set of forces that all pass through one common point, the total turning effect (moment) taken about any chosen point has the same value whichever point is chosen. Reason: If such concurrent forces add up to zero as vectors, their total moment about every point is zero as well.

options.label: (a)
options.text: both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion

options.label: (b)
options.text: both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion

options.label: (c)
options.text: Assertion is true, but the Reason is false

options.label: (d)
options.text: Assertion is false, but the Reason is true

items.question_text:
A three-pulley chain — one pulley fixed to the ceiling, with two lighter pulleys hanging one below the other in series, strung as the figure describes — carries block 1 (mass 1 kg) at the base and block 2 (mass 2 kg) hanging from the lowest pulley's string. The string lengths tie the two accelerations together as a₂ = −7a₁ (block 2 accelerates seven times as fast as block 1, in the opposite sense). Take g = 10 m/s².
(a) Work out how fast each block accelerates.
(b) Work out the pulling force (tension) carried by each string segment.
items.figure_description: A large pulley P₁ is fixed to the ceiling. Below it hang two smaller movable pulleys, P₂ (medium) and P₃ (small), one below the other, and at the bottom sits block 1 (a wide base block); block 2 hangs beside the chain. Three light strings are used. String S₁ passes over P₁: its left end goes straight down to block 1 and its right end goes straight down to the axle of P₂. String S₂ passes over P₂: its left end goes straight down to block 1 and its right end goes straight down to the axle of P₃. String S₃ passes over P₃: its left end goes straight down to block 1 and its right end hangs straight down to block 2. So three string ends are tied to block 1 (one from each pulley) and block 2 hangs from S₃ only. All strings are vertical; pulleys and strings are massless and frictionless. Block 1 has mass 1 kg and block 2 has mass 2 kg. If the tension in S₃ is T, the tensions in S₂ and S₁ are 2T and 4T.

items.question_text: A rod OA hangs from a hinge fixed at point O on a vertical wall. Its lower end, point A, is tied by a weightless string to a fixed point B on a support to the right, at the same height as A. Draw a diagram of the rod alone showing every force acting on it.
items.figure_description: On the left is a vertical wall. Point O is a hinge fixed on this wall, near the top. A rigid rod runs from O down and to the right to its other end, point A. From A, a horizontal massless string runs further right to point B, which is fixed to a second vertical support at the same height as A. The rod slopes downward from the upper-left hinge O to the lower-right end A, and the string AB is horizontal.

items.question_text: In the pulley arrangement shown, block M hangs from a fixed pulley, while a movable pulley, suspended from the other end of the same string, carries a 3 kg block on one side and a 2 kg block on the other. Both pulleys and strings are massless, and there is no friction anywhere. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the value of M for which block M stays at rest.
items.figure_description: A fixed pulley is attached to a rigid support at the top. A string runs over this fixed pulley: block M hangs from one end (the left side), and the other end connects to the axle of a second, movable pulley hanging below it. A second string runs over this movable pulley, with a 3 kg block hanging from its left end and a 2 kg block hanging from its right end.

items.question_text: A 1 kg block sits on a surface that is not smooth. A horizontal pull F acts on the block, as pictured. Taking the static-friction coefficient μₛ = 0.5, the kinetic-friction coefficient μₖ = 0.4, and g = 10 m/s², describe how the friction force f and the block's acceleration a behave as the pull F is raised steadily from zero.
items.figure_description: A block rests on a rough horizontal surface, drawn with hatching to show roughness. A horizontal arrow labeled F, pointing rightward, is applied to the block, pushing it along the surface.

items.question_text: In a pulley arrangement, a ball hangs on one side and a thin rod of length l hangs on the other, with the ball's mass equal to η times the rod's mass. Every pulley and string in the system is weightless, and there is no friction anywhere. At the start the ball sits level with the rod's bottom end, and the system is then let go from rest. Work out how long it takes for the ball to rise level with the rod's top end.
items.figure_description: A pulley is fixed to a bracket on the ceiling. A string passes over the top of this fixed pulley. Its left end hangs straight down to a small ball. Its right end hangs straight down to the axle of a second, smaller pulley, which is not fixed to anything and hangs in the air below and to the right of the fixed pulley, held up only by this string. A second string passes over the top of this hanging pulley, and both of its segments run downward: the left segment goes straight down to the top end of a thin vertical rod of length l, which hangs freely; the right segment goes straight down to a short fixed ledge (bracket) mounted beside the rod, at about the level of the rod's top end. The ball and the rod hang side by side, the ball on the left and the rod on the right. At the moment of release the ball is level with the rod's lower end. The ball's mass is η times the rod's mass; all pulleys and strings are massless and there is no friction.

items.question_text: A 1 kg block and a 2 kg block hang from the two ends of a light, smooth string that passes over a pulley clamped to a fixed support. The system starts from rest and is released. Exactly 1.0 s after release, the 2 kg block (the larger mass) is caught and stopped for an instant, then let go again at once. Find how much time passes after that instant before the string becomes taut again.
items.figure_description: A fixed pulley is clamped at the top. A string over the pulley carries a 1 kg block hanging on one side and a 2 kg block hanging on the other side; the 2 kg block, being heavier, moves down while the 1 kg block moves up.

items.question_text: Starting at the same instant from a common point O, two particles slide down two straight, frictionless wires. The first wire makes an angle of 30° with the vertical, and the second wire makes an angle of 60° with the vertical, both wires lying on the same side of the vertical line through O. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the second particle relative to the first?

A ramp rises from level ground at 60°, the angle being marked at the bottom vertex where the ramp starts. At one point on the ramp's surface four forces act together: an unknown force F directed up along the ramp (parallel to the slope), an unknown force R directed perpendicular to the ramp's surface, away from it, a known force of 3 N pulling horizontally to the left, and a known force of 10 N pulling straight downward. These four forces balance exactly. Work out the values of R and F.
items.figure_description: A ramp rises from a vertex at the lower left toward the upper right, making the marked angle of 60° with the horizontal ground. At one point on the ramp's surface four forces act: F points up the ramp, along the surface toward the upper right; R points perpendicular to the ramp's surface, away from it (up and to the left); a 3 N force points horizontally to the left; a 10 N force points vertically downward.

items.question_text: A ladder of length 4 m and mass 25 kg leans with its top end touching a smooth (frictionless) wall and its bottom end resting on rough ground, making an angle of 60° with the horizontal ground. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the smallest value the coefficient of friction between the ladder and the ground must have so the ladder does not slip.

Starting from rest, a particle is sped up to a velocity v by a force F₁. Afterwards, the same particle is slowed from that same velocity v back down to rest by a different force F₂. Which of these statements about F₁ and F₂ must be true?

options.label: (a)
options.text: F₁ and F₂ are always equal in magnitude

options.label: (b)
options.text: F₂ must be larger than F₁

options.label: (c)
options.text: F₂ could be smaller than, larger than, or equal to F₁

items.question_text: A straight rod AB is pivoted at end A. Three forces act on it, as described below. Determine the anticlockwise moment about the pivot produced by each of the three forces.
items.figure_description: A straight horizontal rod AB is pivoted at its left end A. A force 2F acts vertically upward at a point a distance a from A. A force F acts vertically downward at a point a distance 2a from A. A force 3F acts at the right end B, a distance 4a from A, pointing up and to the left (above the rod, back toward the A side) at 30° to the rod.

items.question_text: Two setups are shown below. In each, someone must lift a block that is currently sitting on the ground up to a height h using a string that passes over one or more pulleys fixed to an overhead support. Both the pulleys and the strings are light (massless) and frictionless. In which setup must the person pull with a greater force, if any?
items.figure_description: Setup (i): a block rests on the ground; a string tied to the block goes straight up, passes over a single pulley fixed to an overhead bracket, and comes down to a person standing beside the block, who pulls the free end. Setup (ii): the same overhead bracket carries one fixed pulley. A second pulley is mounted on a short post fixed to the top of the block, so it moves with the block. The string is tied to the bracket, runs down and passes under the block's pulley, goes back up over the fixed pulley, and comes down to the person, who pulls the free end. In both setups the person pulls the string to raise the block through the same height h.

items.question_text:
A ball weighing 100 N sits at rest on a rough slope tilted 30° from the horizontal; a horizontal cord, running from a point A on the ball to a fixed point B on the slope, keeps the ball from sliding down. Work out the following three quantities.
(a) Find the tension in the cord.
(b) Find the friction force acting on the ball.
(c) Find the normal reaction the slope exerts on the ball.
items.figure_description: An inclined surface rises from the ground at an angle of 30°. A ball rests on this sloped surface, its centre marked C. A horizontal cord runs from point A, the topmost point of the ball (directly above its centre C), to point B, a fixed point on the incline surface farther up the slope at the same height as A, so the cord itself is horizontal and tangent to the ball at A.

items.question_text:
A plank called B, with mass 2m and length l, lies on a horizontal road. A block called A, with mass m, rests on top of plank B at its left-hand edge. The block and the plank are both given the same initial rightward speed v and then move together as a system. Friction acts at two surfaces: road against plank, with coefficient 1/2, and plank against block, with coefficient 1/4. Determine the following.
(a) Find the time that passes before block A slides completely off plank B.
(b) Find how far block A and plank B each travel relative to the ground up to that moment.
items.figure_description: Block A rests on top of plank B, positioned at B's left-hand end; plank B in turn rests on the horizontal road below it. The plank's length, l, runs the full length of B, shown by a measurement arrow beneath it. Both A and B move together to the right with the same initial speed v; the road exerts friction against the plank (coefficient 1/2), and the plank exerts friction against the block (coefficient 1/4).

items.question_text: A man stands still relative to a horizontal conveyor belt, while the belt itself speeds up at 1 m/s². The man's mass is 65 kg, and the coefficient of static friction between his shoes and the belt surface is 0.2. Using g = 9.8 m/s², work out the net force acting on the man. Also work out the largest acceleration the belt can have while the man still stays in place relative to it, without slipping.
items.figure_description: A man stands on the horizontal top surface of a conveyor belt loop; the top surface (where the man stands) moves in one direction while the belt's underside returns in the opposite direction, driven around two end rollers.
